Hi Priya — glad the demo was useful. Short answers up front, followed by specifics and attachments:

1) Where inference is executed (EU customers):
- By default we route requests to compute in the customer-selected region. For Valence Health (EU tenant) requests are executed on EU-hosted GPU pools (Frankfurt or Amsterdam) unless explicitly configured otherwise.

2) Cross-border hops and subprocessors:
- Control plane metadata (request IDs, telemetry) may transit through the Redwood control plane which has nodes in US and EU; control-plane metadata is pseudonymized and does not contain customer prompt content.
- Model execution and ephemeral caches remain in the execution region; we do not route prompt text to non-EU compute for EU-configured tenants.
- Subprocessors: we use managed cloud providers (AWS eu-central-1 / eu-west-1) and a CDN provider for static console assets; their EU regions are used for EU tenants. Non-EU subprocessors are only involved for optional integrations (e.g., marketplace connectors) that you would explicitly enable.

3) Deletion timelines and retention:
- Ephemeral inference state (KV caches, transient logs) is retained for up to 2 hours by default and purged automatically. Customers can configure TTLs.
- Aggregated metrics and non-identifying analytics are retained for 90 days by default (configurable).
- Persistent artifacts (uploaded prompts, training uploads, audit exports) are deleted on request — we provide an erase API and can coordinate an account-level purge; typical completion SLA is 30 days for full deletion across backups and replicas (we include an attestation).

I am attaching a regional dataflow diagram and the extract from our retention/erase playbook. Marissa and Connor are looped for any technical evidence or SOC2 excerpts you might request.

Let me know if you want a focused runbook we can hand to your procurement/security team.

Hi Priya — Marissa here from Compliance/Evidence. Short, factual bullets to support procurement:

- Backups & replication: for EU-configured accounts we keep primary backups in the EU. Cross-region replication to non-EU regions is not performed by default. We offer optional cross-region DR replication (explicit opt-in) which we document in the DPA and only enable with contractual agreement; where enabled, data-at-rest encryption keys are customer-scoped and we support KMS key separation.

- 30-day deletion SLA: our standard erase workflow triggers a coordinated purge across primary stores and snapshots. We provide a deletion attestation within 30 days of request completion. For analytics/quality monitoring stores, only non-identifiable metrics are retained; any metrics containing customer-identifying keys are scrubbed as part of the purge. If you require a shorter contractual window we can discuss an accelerated erasure addendum (subject to engineering rollback windows).

- Evidence: see attached extract (redwood-delete-retention-extract-2028.pdf) for the DPA clauses and a sample deletion attestation form. Our SOC2 report (available under NDA) also maps to the controls referenced in the extract; happy to start the NDA if needed.
